subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw extend `steer` into a true abort/resume soft-steer lifecycle, or keep `steer` boundary-based and add any stronger behavior as an explicit opt-in mode or command?
rationale: The choice affects default queue semantics, transcript ordering, tool-call completion guarantees, and user-visible compatibility, so automation should not pick the permanent product contract.

options.title: Keep boundary steer; design opt-in soft-steer
options.body: Preserve current `steer` semantics, land the ordinary-message admission fix separately, and require a new explicit mode or command for abort/resume behavior.

options.title: Make steer interrupt/resume by default
options.body: Change the default behavior to abort and resume active turns when possible, accepting the compatibility and transcript-ordering risk as intended product direction.

options.title: Defer true soft-steer
options.body: Document boundary steering as the supported contract for now and close or split this tracker after the narrower active-run admission issue is resolved.

recommendation.title: Keep boundary steer; design opt-in soft-steer
recommendation.body: Preserve current `steer` semantics, land the ordinary-message admission fix separately, and require a new explicit mode or command for abort/resume behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are connected to recent steering semantics and adjacent terminal-session lifecycle work that the decision must preserve.
